I recently went hiking in #California, and my family were * thrilled * when I started talking about California geological history and want it means for my day job in #energy.

Some of the oldest rocks in California are over 1.5 billion years old. (The world 'billion' also makes sense outside of the state's Silicon Valley too!). Layered up over time, they've formed sediments of mud, fossils, stones, and dirt. And what else has this kind of layering I hear you ask? (I'm pretty sure you asked...?).

Our Digital Energy Stack!

As the AI 'race' reaffirms how energy is both a key driver of sustainable development and #21stCentury industrial policy, energy needs to be much more intertwined with how we develop and deploy digital. This is the thinking behind our stack. Identifying - and supporting countries and communities to implement - the tech (and non-tech) elements needed to unlock the combined power and potential of digital and energy.

We'd love your reflections on this. The seven layers we've identified are:

1️⃣ Data - crucial for energy planning, optimisation, and measuring energy inclusion.

2️⃣ Connectivity - including the potential of shared business models, such as PAYG solar.

3️⃣ Compute - processing power to shape energy inclusion planning, but also a resource that needs to be carefully shaped alongside domestic energy supply.

4️⃣ Digital Public Infrastructure - our digital roads and railways, which can improve energy access through better credit scoring and improved data exchange.

5️⃣ Cybersecurity - protecting energy assets which are critical national infrastructure. 

6️⃣ AI - already improving grid planning, and also providing opportunities to better connect under-served communities.

And(!), 7️⃣ governance. Digital is just a tool in our energy toolkit. We need to build the skills, expertise, and institutions to make this strategic thinking happen.
